text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd said Thursday it filed a defamation lawsuit against Consumers Union, publisher of Consumer Reports magazine.

At a news conference here, Isuzu officials claimed Consumers Union and its technical dirrector David Pittle defamed Isuzu and disparaged the company's Trooper sport utility vehicle by making false statements about the safety of the 1995 and 1996 models.

The suit, filed in federal district court in Los Angeles, cites a decision last week by the U.S. Department of Transportation's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) to rule against Consumer Union's petition for a defect investigation of the Trooper.
Consumer Union's petition was based on its repeated claim that the Trooper has a unique propensity to roll over during real-world driving maneuvers.

Officials from Isuzu declined to say the amount of the compensatory and punitive damages the company would seek from Consumers Union but said it would easily stretch into the "many millions of dollars" and would likely be one of the largest defamation suits brought by an automaker against the publication.
An attorney for Isuzu alleged Consumers Union staged a series of tests last summer to make the Trooper tip over using maneuvers that would never be used in a real-world situation.
"If you ever caught your kid driving that way, you'd send him to bed without supper, you'd spank him and you'd take away his keys for a month," said attorney Richard Bowman.

Terry Maloney, senior vice president and general manager of light-vehicles for American Isuzu Motors, said sales of the Trooper in the first six months of this year were down 54 percent from the year ago period largely as a result of the publicity from the Consumer Reports article.
Isuzu said it will also be requesting Consumers Union to turn over all its secret files on this entire episode.
